children: The dollar briefly hits a seven-week high against a basket of currencies before paring gains as oil prices swing. Crude prices turn lower after Japan's Kyodo News said Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the U.S. takes steps toward easing military pressure. An earlier rise in oil prices, which reflected continuing shipping risks, had lifted the dollar due to the U.S.'s position as a net oil exporter and the currency's safe-haven role. Meanwhile, markets are betting on further U.S. interest-rate rises after the Federal Reserve raised rates by a quarter point last week and signaled further moves. The DXY dollar index rises 0.1% to 100.514 after reaching as high as 100.667 earlier. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
